ranking_release.note: Ranking readiness verifies data schema, ordering and rank integrity only. It does not establish independent scientific accuracy or planetary analog validity.

global_scan.coverage_definition: Fraction of Copernicus GLO-90 tileList land tiles whose elevation COG was opened and processed. Ocean has no DEM tile; this is not a claim of ocean coverage.

moon.interpretation: This diagnostic compares two different feature families derived from the same Copernicus GLO-90 source within the retained primary shortlist. It tests rank sensitivity to feature choice; it is not independent-source validation, model accuracy, field truth or a calibrated probability.

mars.interpretation: This diagnostic compares two different feature families derived from the same Copernicus GLO-90 source within the retained primary shortlist. It tests rank sensitivity to feature choice; it is not independent-source validation, model accuracy, field truth or a calibrated probability.

interpretation: Global terrain screening is complete only for the enumerated Copernicus GLO-90 land-tile inventory. The stored list is a bounded shortlist, not all evaluated windows. Primary rank uses the core terrain family only; the alternative family is diagnostic. Neither score is a probability, calibrated accuracy or analog verdict.

independent_analog_label_validation.note: No independently sourced, reviewed positive/negative analog label file is present. No AUC or accuracy is inferred.

global_land_cover_enrichment.interpretation: 2023 Sentinel-2-derived land-cover context for retained shortlist windows only; not geology or field truth.

scope.coverage_note: Enrichment is limited to the retained top-100-per-target terrain shortlist, deduplicated by candidate window ID; it is not a global climate raster or all-window climate scan.

global_nasa_power_climatology.interpretation: NASA POWER gridded climatology at retained candidate coordinates, not in-situ observations or a full global climate raster.

source.version: GLiM v1.1 simplified ArcGIS FeatureServer layer
source.license: CC BY 3.0 (PANGAEA gridded GLiM record; confirm terms for the served v1.1 derivative before redistribution)
source.attribution: Hartmann, J. and N. Moosdorf (2012), The new global lithological map database GLiM: A representation of rock properties at the Earth's surface, Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems, 13, Q12004.

method.operation: Point-in-polygon lookup at approximate centre of each retained 5.55 km GLO-90 terrain window
method.role: Contextual geology evidence only; excluded from all terrain ranking and scoring.

limitations: GLiM is a generalized compilation of regional geological maps; the paper reports an average mapping scale around 1:3,750,000 and the original database is assembled from many national/regional sources.
The returned class is the polygon intersecting the approximate window centre, not an area-weighted lithology mixture across the full 5.55 km window.
No local rock exposure, regolith, mineralogy, soil chemistry, alteration, geotechnical properties or field observations are measured.
Boundary position, source-map scale, compilation and regional mapping coverage can affect the class returned at a point.
This enrichment is applied only to the retained top-100-per-target shortlist, deduplicated by candidate ID; it is not a global lithology raster reprocessing of all 5.85 million terrain windows.
A missing feature is reported as no_feature_returned; it is not converted into a lithology class.
global_lithology_context.interpretation: Generalized GLiM centre-point context for retained candidates only. Not area-weighted, field-verified geology; excluded from candidate scoring.

independent_dem_crosscheck.source: NASADEM (SRTM-derived) compared with Copernicus DEM GLO-30 DSM
limits: NASADEM has approximate coverage from 56°S to 60°N; high-latitude sites such as McMurdo, Haughton or Iceland may be outside its coverage.
NASADEM uses SRTM with auxiliary void filling and is not a perfect independent ground survey.
NASADEM and Copernicus GLO-30 have different acquisition sensors, processing and DSM/DEM semantics; compare coarse descriptors, not absolute elevation datums.
This is independent raster-source checking, not in-situ field validation, geological validation or planetary analog validation.
Rank correlation is only descriptive for this small, selected set and must not be presented as calibrated model accuracy.
independent_dem_crosscheck.interpretation: Independent elevation-source check on a small selected overlap set; not field validation or a global accuracy estimate.

ground_truth_validation.note: Physical field validation can only be claimed for properties and locations covered by documented measurements and independent review. Protocols, proposed stations and desk data do not count.

limitations: SHA-256 establishes byte-level identity, not scientific validity or source authenticity.
The manifest records the repository commit before its own final commit; it cannot hash its final committed bytes.
Historical external retrieval metadata may be incomplete and must be traced through source registry and product-specific records.

evidence_registry.rule: browse_only, metadata_only and reference_only records are not represented as fully processed quantitative science inputs.

release_gate.ranking_release: ready only when schema 1.1.0 core-only ordering and rank-integrity checks pass
release_gate.independent_analog_validation: awaiting independently sourced, reviewed labels and spatially blocked held-out evaluation
release_gate.global_scan: complete only when every enumerated land tile is processed and tile_failures=0
release_gate.quantitative_validation: diagnostic-only until independent labels, spatially blocked tests and defensible held-out validation are available
release_gate.field_validation: requires georeferenced observations, instrument/calibration provenance, permissions and independent review
release_gate.data_depth: each source retains a state; browse images and catalogue metadata are not decoded science arrays
release_gate.reproducibility: manifest and per-product source/method/parameter/provenance records required; hashes alone do not prove validity
